versions.changelog:
- Version updated to 19.0.0 with corresponding metadata changes.
- Added distribution-manifest.json to support distribution and version tracking.
- Removed skill-card.md from the project.
- No changes to core functionality or usage instructions.

Version 18.0.0 (narrative-registry)

- Bumped version to 18.0.0.
- Updated SKILL.md metadata (notably the version value in the metadata object).
- Removed the file skill-card.md.
- No changes to instructions, features, or workflow in SKILL.md content.

Major refactor: Narrative registry is now an event-sourced, versioned, protocol skill for atomic canon updates and explicit proposal/accept flows.

- Canon versions are now managed as complete, atomic events in an append-only narrative event stream.
- Human-facing files (`canon.md`/`versions.md`) are generated views, not hand-maintained ledgers.
- All updates require full canon objects (no partial/patch edits); incomplete or inconsistent versions are rejected.
- Records include detailed provenance, version/revision info, claim/proof pointers, and unresolved contradictions.
- All writes must pass through the verified host runtime with owner capability checks; no direct file/NDJSON edits.
- Proposal handling, capability security, downstream consumption, and handoff summary instructions clarified and standardized.
- Two supporting skill files removed to streamline contract.

narrative-registry 16.0.0

- Full rewrite and clarification of the skill's scope, purpose, and contract, emphasizing strict protocol-layer registry responsibilities.
- More explicit delineation between this skill and narrative-quality-auditor, message-system-architect, offer-claims-registry, and related skills.
- Improved documentation of versioning logic: atomic canon re-versioning and append-only history, with detailed process notes.
- Expanded guidance on what to record/promote (full canon facts, version history, intake candidate promotion) and what *not* to do (no veto scoring, message house authoring, or claim adjudication).
- Concise plain-language instructions and examples for intake, re-versioning, and candidate promotion.
- Clarifies all key skill boundaries for interoperability within complex brand narrative systems.
